headline: Funds the federal government through September 2025, mostly at 2024 levels, and extends many expiring health and other programs.
what_it_does: This law keeps federal agencies funded for the rest of fiscal year 2025, which ends September 30, 2025, and avoids a government shutdown. Most programs get the same funding as in 2024, with some raised or cut. It also extends many health programs, Medicare payment rules, and other expiring authorities, most through September 30, 2025.

who_it_affects.how: Agencies keep operating for the rest of fiscal year 2025, mostly at 2024 funding levels.

who_it_affects.group: People on Medicare who use telehealth
who_it_affects.how: They can keep getting covered telehealth visits from home, including some audio-only visits, through fiscal year 2025.
Funding continues for health centers that serve areas with few medical providers.

who_it_affects.group: Health care providers in shortage areas
who_it_affects.how: National Health Service Corps scholarships and loan repayment awards continue to be funded.

who_it_affects.group: Small rural hospitals and rural ambulance services
who_it_affects.how: They keep receiving certain extra Medicare payments through fiscal year 2025.

who_it_affects.group: Hospitals that serve many low-income patients
who_it_affects.how: Planned cuts to their extra Medicaid payments are delayed until fiscal year 2026.
The Special Diabetes Program for Indians, which supports diabetes treatment and prevention, keeps its funding.
Funding continues for research on preventing and curing Type 1 diabetes.

who_it_affects.group: Families of children with special health care needs
who_it_affects.how: Grants continue for family-run groups that offer them information and peer support.

who_it_affects.group: Young people in sex education programs
who_it_affects.how: Two federal programs, one focused on avoiding sex outside marriage and one covering abstinence and contraception, continue through fiscal year 2025.

who_it_affects.group: People convicted of certain sex abuse or human trafficking crimes
who_it_affects.how: They must still pay a special fee that funds programs for trafficking survivors.

who_it_affects.group: People who make or sell fentanyl-related substances
who_it_affects.how: These substances stay classified as Schedule I drugs, the strictest legal category.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted March 15, 2025; most funding and extensions run through September 30, 2025 (end of fiscal year 2025).
